title: In three fly antennal-lobe connectomes, the local-neuron inhibition pattern of a glomerulus did not explain its projection-neuron odour responses better than the pattern of other glomeruli
abstract: We tested if glomerulus-specific inhibitory local-neuron (LN) wiring in the Drosophila antennal lobe explains projection-neuron (PN) odour responses. We used PN calcium responses of Badel et al. (2016) for 30 single odours, DoOR 2.0 receptor responses as the input to each glomerulus, and LN disynaptic wiring from FlyWire left and right antennal lobes (one fly) and the hemibrain right antennal lobe (a second fly). For 21 glomeruli, we fitted the PN response from its own receptor input and measured the partial correlation with an inhibition pool: the input of the other glomeruli with equal weights or with connectome weights. The equal-weight pool had a positive partial correlation (mean +0.16, 95% CI +0.07 to +0.24), so the data did not show net global suppression. The connectome pool was less positive (difference -0.043, -0.055, -0.030; p = 0.047, 0.014, 0.085 against independent per-row permutation), which passed our pre-specified rule in the two FlyWire hemispheres. But post-hoc controls showed that this is not target-specific: the LN row of a random other glomerulus fit equally well (p = 0.59, 0.50, 0.80), and one source weighting shared by all targets gave the same values and was not better than permuted source weights (p = 0.10, 0.08, 0.11). The connectome pool did not improve leave-one-odour-out prediction, and the inhibitory load of a glomerulus did not predict its pool sensitivity (rho +0.08, +0.09). LN pool rows agreed between connectomes (rho 0.91 within FlyWire, 0.42 to 0.43 with hemibrain). Limitations: one PN dataset, unmatched odour concentrations, DoOR as input proxy, single odours only, hemibrain without traced ORNs, several post-hoc tests.
